answer: We formulate a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds create a capital canyon, ensuring that the marginal utility of identity multiplication remains below the nadir of legitimate participation. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices enforce a slashing regime where any adversarial zephyr of fraudulent actors triggers immediate collateral forfeiture. This configuration renders the expected payoff of Sybil attacks strictly negative, forcing convergence toward a unique Nash equilibrium in multi-agent environments.
